## Purpose and entry points
NumPy is a scientific-computing library for Python centered on the N-dimensional `ndarray`, vectorized operations, and numerical subsystems. User imports enter through `numpy/__init__.py`; the implementation-facing core namespace is `numpy/_core/__init__.py`, while legacy/public compatibility forwarding remains under `numpy/core/__init__.py`. A CLI entry point exists for Fortran wrapping at `numpy/f2py/__main__.py`.

## Array core and ABI boundary
The core is Python API plus compiled C/C++ extension modules built from `numpy/_core/meson.build`. Array construction, layout, indexing, iteration, casting, descriptors/dtypes, and module state live in `numpy/_core/src/multiarray/`, notably `arrayobject.c`, `ctors.c`, and `descriptor.c`. Public C APIs and ABI-facing headers are exposed from `numpy/_core/include/numpy/arrayobject.h`, `ndarrayobject.h`, and `dtype_api.h`; these form a critical compatibility boundary for native extensions.

## Ufunc execution pipeline
High-level numerical calls resolve to universal functions (ufuncs), which select dtype-specific loops and execute strided elementwise or reduction kernels. Python-facing bindings are in `numpy/_core/umath.py`; compiled dispatch, type resolution, and loop machinery are in `numpy/_core/src/umath/ufunc_object.c`, `ufunc_type_resolution.c`, and generated/dispatchable loop sources such as `loops_arithmetic.dispatch.c.src`. Overrides provide interoperability with non-NumPy array types through `numpy/_core/overrides.py` and `numpy/_core/src/common/ufunc_override.c`.

## Dtypes, coercion, and array protocols
Input Python objects, buffers, and array-like providers are normalized into arrays through coercion and conversion code (`numpy/_core/src/multiarray/array_coercion.c`, `convert_datatype.c`). The dtype system determines storage, casts, scalar promotion, and loop eligibility; its public and internal implementations span `numpy/dtypes.py`, `numpy/_core/src/multiarray/dtypemeta.c`, and `numpy/_core/src/multiarray/abstractdtypes.c`. Interchange boundaries include the buffer protocol, DLPack (`numpy/_core/src/multiarray/dlpack.c`), and array-function dispatch.

## Performance portability
NumPy compiles architecture-specific kernels and chooses supported CPU implementations at runtime. Build-time CPU configuration is organized in `meson_cpu/meson.build` and architecture directories such as `meson_cpu/x86/meson.build`; runtime feature detection and dispatch reside in `numpy/_core/src/common/npy_cpu_features.c` and `npy_cpu_dispatch.c`. Portable SIMD abstractions and ISA backends are in `numpy/_core/src/common/simd/`; generated SIMD Python bindings are under `numpy/_core/src/_simd/`.

## Numerical subsystems
Specialized packages build on `ndarray` and compiled kernels: FFT uses Python wrappers plus PocketFFT (`numpy/fft/_pocketfft.py`, `numpy/fft/_pocketfft_umath.cpp`); linear algebra wraps BLAS/LAPACK-compatible operations (`numpy/linalg/_linalg.py`, `numpy/linalg/umath_linalg.cpp`); random exposes Cython-backed generators and C bit generators (`numpy/random/_generator.pyx`, `numpy/random/src/pcg64/pcg64.c`). External BLAS/LAPACK selection is a material build/runtime dependency, with bundled `lapack_lite` fallback sources present.

## Native-language integration and build delivery
F2PY parses Fortran signatures/source and generates Python extension bindings, then delegates builds through backend abstractions including Meson: `numpy/f2py/f2py2e.py`, `numpy/f2py/_backends/_meson.py`, and `numpy/f2py/src/fortranobject.c`. The project uses Meson as the primary native build graph (`meson.build`, `numpy/meson.build`) and `pyproject.toml` for Python packaging. CI targets native platforms, SIMD, BLAS, sanitizers, WebAssembly/Emscripten, and wheel production via `.github/workflows/` and `tools/wheels/`.
